# Kamino klend-sdk and REST API — facts

## How it works

- [statement] Kamino's selection guidance: use the REST API for vault lists with APR and TVL, APY charts, a user's historical rewards, client-side signing flows and non-JS backends such as Python. Use the TypeScript SDK for fully customized transaction execution, simulation and vault creation, and when the integration must 'Require zero rate limits' (SDK with a private RPC). SDK reads need a private RPC or the rate-limited public endpoint. (high confidence) — https://kamino.com/docs/build/developers/api-vs-sdk.md · keywords: Kamino klend-sdk and REST API · also: https://kamino.com/docs/build/developers/borrow/data/market-data.md
- [statement] In klend-sdk's vault builders, the optional payer argument is the rent payer for ATAs the instructions create, not the transaction fee payer. The Solana Foundation integration renamed the field rentPayer to keep the two apart, because its gasless fee-payer path sets the fee payer separately at compile time. (low confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/solana-foundation/solana-developer-platform/main/packages/sdp-kamino/CLAUDE.md · keywords: Kamino klend-sdk and REST API

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] The slot duration passed to KaminoMarket.load drives fixed-rate APY math. Kamino's docs say a hard-coded 400 ms shows fixed-rate APYs at about half their real rate, because mainnet slots are closer to 210 ms. They tell callers to pass await getMedianSlotDurationInMsFromLastEpochs(). (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://kamino.com/docs/build/borrow/get-market-reserve-apys.md · keywords: Kamino klend-sdk and REST API · also: https://kamino.com/docs/build/developers/borrow/data/market-data.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The data API's OpenAPI description says 'The API is rate-limited for unauthenticated users. If you feel you need to make more requests or run into rate-limit issues, please reach out.' Kamino's docs index says 'No API key required for public endpoints.' Neither OpenAPI document defines a security scheme, and no request thresholds are published. Rate limits and auth belong to a sibling concept. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://api.kamino.finance/openapi/json?openapi=3.0.0 · keywords: Kamino klend-sdk and REST API · also: https://kamino.com/docs/llms.txt, https://api.kamino.finance/ktx/documentation/json
- [statement] REST paths mix unversioned, /v2 and /v3 prefixes. Kamino's APY recipe lists markets at GET /v2/kamino-market but reads reserve metrics at the unversioned GET /kamino-market/{pubkey}/reserves/metrics. The data spec marks two operations deprecated, GET /v2/kamino-market/{marketPubkey}/obligations/{obligationPubkey}/interest-fees and .../interest-paid; /v3 versions of both exist. The spec gives no sunset dates. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://api.kamino.finance/openapi/json?openapi=3.0.0 · keywords: Kamino klend-sdk and REST API · also: https://kamino.com/docs/build/borrow/get-market-reserve-apys.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] klend-sdk converts every Decimal to mint atoms and floors silently. A value finer than the mint (for example 1.0000009 on a six-decimal mint) moves only 1.000000 on chain, and a minSharesOut below one atom becomes 0, which gives no slippage protection. The Solana Foundation integration rejects values finer than the mint instead of clamping them. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/solana-foundation/solana-developer-platform/main/packages/sdp-kamino/CLAUDE.md · keywords: Kamino klend-sdk and REST API

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Kamino offers three programmatic surfaces for Kamino Lend. The REST API (base URL https://api.kamino.finance) serves data, analytics and unsigned transactions in any language. The TypeScript SDK @kamino-finance/klend-sdk reads on-chain state and builds transactions, in TS/JS only. The Rust klend-interface crate is a lightweight instruction builder for Rust clients, bots and on-chain CPI. (high confidence) — https://kamino.com/docs/build/developers/api-vs-sdk.md · keywords: Kamino klend-sdk and REST API · also: https://kamino.com/docs/skill.md
- [statement] History exists only in the REST API. Kamino's docs say 'Historical market data is only available via the API', and the SDK has 'No history tracking. Developers must persist snapshots manually if needed.' Vault creation is the reverse case: only the SDK has the admin tools. The SDK reads live account state over RPC. (high confidence) — https://kamino.com/docs/build/developers/api-vs-sdk.md · keywords: Kamino klend-sdk and REST API · also: https://kamino.com/docs/build/developers/borrow/data/market-data.md
- [statement] The REST API returns an unsigned transaction that the caller must sign client-side. The SDK returns instructions that the caller assembles, signs and sends. Either way the signing key stays with the caller. (high confidence) — https://kamino.com/docs/build/developers/api-vs-sdk.md · keywords: Kamino klend-sdk and REST API · also: https://kamino.com/docs/build/borrow/recipes/deposit-via-api.md
- [statement] Kamino's developer docs are built for agents. Every page is fetchable as raw markdown by appending .md, https://kamino.com/docs/llms.txt indexes all pages, and https://kamino.com/docs/skill.md lists endpoints and SDK calls for each product. The Solana Foundation's integration note tells agents to start from skill.md and not to answer Kamino questions from memory. (medium confidence) — https://kamino.com/docs/llms.txt · keywords: Kamino klend-sdk and REST API · also: https://kamino.com/docs/skill.md, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/solana-foundation/solana-developer-platform/main/packages/sdp-kamino/CLAUDE.md
- [statement] The klend-sdk repo includes a CLI. The README shows 'yarn cli deposit --url <RPC> --owner ./keypair.json --token SOL --amount 10' and commands that print lending-market and reserve account data. Kamino's skill file says the Kamino CLI via the Klend SDK can create and manage curator vaults. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/Kamino-Finance/klend-sdk · keywords: Kamino klend-sdk and REST API · also: https://kamino.com/docs/skill.md
